calls.title: Designing Experiments for Long-Term Growth
calls.summary: The discussion emphasized the necessity of experimentation due to low success rates of initiatives, with major companies reporting around 10-15% success. Ronny Kohavi highlighted randomized controlled experiments as essential for understanding true impacts while acknowledging the risks of false positives. The unpredictability of outcomes was illustrated by significant gains from minor changes, reinforcing the need for testing. Companies are encouraged to develop composite metrics that reflect long-term goals, balancing revenue and user satisfaction. Additionally, the dangers of shipping flat results were addressed, advocating for a culture that values measurable impacts. Continuous validation of proxy metrics ensures alignment with long-term objectives, while the frequentist approach to statistics was preferred for online experiments.
calls.keywords: Experimentation, Overall Evaluation Criterion, A/B Testing, Shipping Flat, Surrogate Metrics, Long-Term Growth
